content: According to BIBREF4, much of the prior research describes “extremely negative evaluations of others" as a major component of dehumanization. This is especially pronounced in BIBREF20's account of delegitimization, which involves using negative characteristics to categorize groups that are “excluded from the realm of acceptable norms and values" BIBREF20. While BIBREF20 defines delegitimization as a distinct process, he considers dehumanization to be one means of delegitimization. BIBREF13 also discusses broader processes of moral exclusion, one of which is dehumanization. A closely related process is psychological distancing, in which one perceives others to be objects or nonexistent BIBREF13. BIBREF21 identifies elements that contribute to the objectification (and thus dehumanization) of women, one of which is denial of subjectivity, or the habitual neglect of one's experiences, emotions, and feelings.
